author_dataset: Author-reported scRNA-seq analysis (specific GEO accession not stated in the text; cited as 'ScRNA-seq analysis' with references [56,57])
author_finding: The two hub genes SPP1 and APOE were "significantly enriched in macrophages"
our_dataset: GSE81861 (this study's z-score attribution, a different dataset from the authors')
agreement: Fully concordant (2/2 genes, exact cell-type match)
note: This model's theme is lipid metabolism + ER stress, not an explicitly immune/TME-named theme, yet its genes were independently attributed to macrophages by two different methods and two different datasets -- a strong piece of corroborating evidence for non-tautology (the candidate pool was not pre-restricted to a cell type).

author_finding: CA9 mainly expressed in fibroblasts; PLAU mainly expressed in fibroblasts and macrophages; SLC2A1 broadly highly expressed in fibroblasts, macrophages, T cells, and B cells
our_dataset: PAAD_GSE154778 (this study's z-score attribution, a different dataset from the authors')
agreement: Partially concordant (1/3; PLAU→Fibroblasts is an exact match; CA9 and SLC2A1 were attributed to Malignant in this study, inconsistent with the authors' reported stromal/immune cells)
note: The 2 discordant genes likely reflect differences in candidate cell-type distribution / malignant-cell proportion between the two datasets (different patient cohorts), not a contradiction of the method itself; this discrepancy is candidly recorded rather than citing only the 1 concordant gene.

author_dataset: GSE189357 (author-reported scRNA dataset, with 9 broad cell categories)
author_finding: PPP1R14B mainly expressed in monocytes, macrophages, and endothelial cells; PLEK2 mainly expressed in monocytes; RHOV mainly expressed in endothelial cells
our_dataset: NSCLC_GSE131907 (this study's z-score attribution; this dataset is one of the candidate-type-coverage-incomplete datasets already documented in Sections 3.5/5, annotating only 3 broad immune-cell categories -- CD4Tconv/B/CD8T -- with no myeloid, endothelial, or malignant cells)
agreement: Discordant at the cell-subtype level (0/3 exact matches), but partially concordant at the category level -- the monocytes/macrophages/endothelial cells the authors report are all TME cells (Immune_Hematopoietic/Stromal_Vascular), directionally consistent with this study's H1a TME-concentration logic; this study's z-score result falls on CD4/CD8T, likewise TME/immune cells rather than tumor cells, just a different specific subtype
note: This discrepancy is concrete evidence for the already-documented limitation of NSCLC_GSE131907's incomplete candidate-type coverage (missing myeloid/endothelial/malignant candidates): with a more completely-covered dataset (the authors' GSE189357), these genes are attributed to candidate types that do not exist at all in this study's reference atlas for this dataset (monocytes, endothelial cells), suggesting the attribution result under this study's dataset is systematically constrained by the missing candidate types, and it cannot be excluded that these genes' "true" TME-cell assignment is masked by this study's dataset coverage gap.

theme: Metastasis/basement-membrane-related (candidate-pool non-tautology, verified and logged in 15_cross_theme_meta_analysis.py)
author_dataset: GSE129845 (single-cell) + spatial transcriptomics (2 independent specimens) + multiplex immunofluorescence (the candidate pool was built using DEG ∩ metastasis genes ∩ basement-membrane genes, not restricted to CAF; the single-cell analysis was an independent downstream validation performed after the candidate pool was already fixed)
author_finding: DDR2 and SERPINF1 (2 of the 6 genes) were consistently shown, across three orthogonal methods -- single-cell, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence -- to be preferentially expressed in CAFs/fibroblasts rather than epithelial tumor cells
our_dataset: BLCA_GSE130001 (this study's z-score attribution, a different dataset from the authors')
agreement: Fully concordant (2/2 genes, exact cell-type match)
note: This is the strongest non-tautology corroboration case found in this mining exercise: the candidate pool itself was not pre-restricted to CAF genes by single-cell analysis (already verified and excluded as tautology in 15_cross_theme_meta_analysis.py), and the model's theme is not an explicit TME-cell name either (it is a pathway-oriented name, "metastasis/basement membrane") -- yet two genes were independently attributed to CAFs/fibroblasts by the authors' three orthogonal methods (single-cell + spatial + IHC) and by this study's z-score method on a different dataset. This is genuine cross-team, cross-dataset, cross-method corroboration, disconnected from the mechanism implied by the name "metastasis-related genes."

author_dataset: Author-reported scRNA-seq analysis (based on the TISCH database, no single specific GEO accession given)
author_finding: TUFM, IFI35, and TAPBP mainly expressed in tumor cells; CD53 and TAPBP mainly expressed in B cells; CLEC2D mainly expressed in CD4+ T cells; SOD2 mainly expressed in monocytes and macrophages
our_dataset: SKCM_GSE120575 (this study's z-score attribution, a different dataset from the authors')
agreement: Partially concordant (SOD2→Mono/Macro is an exact match; TUFM and CD53 were attributed to different cell types between the two methods)
note: This model's 9-gene panel itself shows heterogeneity (some genes tumor cells, some immune cells), and the authors' own report does not show a single concentrated pattern either; this is candidly recorded as a mixed case, not forced into either H1a or H1b.

author_dataset: Author-reported scRNA-seq analysis (no specific GEO accession given)
author_finding: HMGCS2 mainly expressed in hepatocytes; FABP5 mainly enriched in myeloid cells
our_dataset: GSE151530 (this study's z-score attribution, a different dataset from the authors')
agreement: Concordant at the category level (2/2; hepatocytes ≈ this study's malignant-cell category, myeloid cells ≈ this study's TAMs category)
note: This model's theme is cholesterol metabolism; HMGCS2's concentration in malignant cells itself matches biological expectation for a metabolism-related gene (not a disconnect), while FABP5's concentration in TAMs echoes the H1a logic -- both patterns coexist within the same model, indicating that whether a "disconnect" exists must be judged gene by gene, not generalized across an entire model.

author_dataset: GSE210679 (author-reported scRNA-seq dataset) + functional knockdown experiments (autophagic activity, proliferation, and migration were all suppressed after ATIC silencing)
author_finding: ATIC is significantly enriched in tumor cells and positively correlated with autophagic activity; functional experiments confirmed that ATIC silencing does affect autophagy-related phenotypes
our_dataset: GSE151530 (this study's z-score attribution, a different dataset from the authors')
agreement: Fully concordant (1/1, exact cell-type match), with independent functional-experiment support
note: **An important balancing case, not evidence hand-picked to support the hypothesis**: this model's theme is autophagy; ATIC's concentration in malignant cells itself, together with functional knockdown experiments confirming its mechanistic role in autophagy within tumor cells, is a positive case where "naming and mechanism are not disconnected." This shows that the author-reported single-cell observations mined in this study do not uniformly support the "disconnect" hypothesis, and including this counter-example candidly is necessary to avoid selectively citing only confirming evidence.
